title: Detecting Emergent Intersectional Biases: Contextualized Word Embeddings Contain a Distribution of Human-like Biases

bias_targets.methodology: Using Intersectional Bias Detection (IBD) and Emergent Intersectional Bias Detection (EIBD) to identify bias attributes from static embeddings, then applying the Contextualized Embedding Association Test (CEAT) to measure the distribution of effect sizes of these biases in contextualized word embeddings.

Applying the Contextualized Embedding Association Test (CEAT) to measure the differential associations of target group names (e.g., European American, African American, Mexican American) with evaluative polar attribute words (e.g., pleasant vs. unpleasant).

Applying the Contextualized Embedding Association Test (CEAT) to measure the differential associations of male and female names/terms with attributes related to career vs. family, math vs. arts, and science vs. arts.
Applying the Contextualized Embedding Association Test (CEAT) to measure the differential associations of young and old people's names with pleasant vs. unpleasant attribute words.
Applying the Contextualized Embedding Association Test (CEAT) to measure the differential associations of mental and physical diseases with temporary vs. permanent attributes.
